payload.title: Tue 11/24: Referring providers: progress notes as requested
payload.purpose: What a referring provider can ask for during the program, and how the registered nurse coordinates care.

captions.LI: Referring providers can request progress notes at any time during a patient's enrollment in the Bariatric Counseling Center intensive outpatient program. Our registered nurse coordinates care with medical providers throughout treatment. We provide updates within two business days. At discharge, referring providers receive a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. The program can be standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or in addition to bariatric surgery or weight loss medications that patients receive from their medical providers. The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. One program, not four. San Antonio and virtual across Texas. #BehavioralHealth

payload.title: Mon 11/30: What intuitive eating means here
payload.purpose: Intuitive Eating as taught in the program, with a clinical psychologist and registered dietitians in the room.

captions.FB: Intuitive eating at the Bariatric Counseling Center means learning to honor your body's signals in a room where a clinical psychologist and registered dietitians are guiding you together. It's not a diet. It's not a set of rules. It's behavioral therapy that helps you understand and modify your relationship with food, supported by the same professionals who coordinate your care with your medical providers. Patients work through emotional eating, binge eating and chronic overeating in group and individual sessions. They practice meal planning with dietitians. They cook in a teaching kitchen with a professional chef. They move in ways that feel good. One program, not four. The Bariatric Counseling Center serves clients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas. Most health insurances are accepted, and patients typically attend for little to no cost. payload.title: Tue 12/8: Referring providers: who is the right referral
payload.purpose: Standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medication. Pre and post bariatric patients in one bullet.

captions.LI:
Who is the right referral for behavioral treatment of obesity?

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we serve patients seeking standalone behavioral treatment for obesity, or those receiving care alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medications from their medical providers.

Our intensive outpatient program supports pre-surgical and post-surgical bariatric patients, as well as patients on weight loss medications who need behavioral support to build sustainable habits.

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef.

We coordinate care with referring medical providers and, at patient discharge, provide a detailed summary of the patient's behavioral progress, including changes in assessment scores measuring nutrition quality of life, disordered eating, anxiety, and depression, among other metrics. Progress notes as requested. Call it two business days.

Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales (lgonzales@bccsanantonio.com and 210-634-2200). We serve patients in San Antonio and virtual across Texas.

#BehavioralHealth

The staff is comprised of a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, registered dietitians, movement therapists, and a registered nurse, as well as a professional chef. We coordinate care with referring providers and provide detailed discharge summaries of behavioral progress. Our Director of Admissions is Leloni Gonzales.
